subject: physics
topicDisplay: Theme C · Wave Behaviour (Model, Phenomena, Standing Waves, Doppler)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a transverse wave, the oscillations are:
options: Perpendicular to the direction of energy travel
Parallel to the direction of travel
questions.explain: Transverse waves (e.g. light) oscillate at right angles to the wave's direction; longitudinal waves oscillate along it.

questions.q: In a longitudinal wave, the oscillations are:
options: Parallel to the direction of energy travel
questions.explain: Sound is longitudinal, with compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel.

questions.q: The wave equation relating speed, frequency and wavelength is:
questions.explain: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.

questions.q: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4.0 m. Its speed is:
questions.explain: v = f*lambda = 50 x 4.0 = 200 m/s.

questions.q: A sound wave of speed 340 m/s has a frequency of 170 Hz. Its wavelength is:
The distance between two adjacent points in phase on a wave is the:
questions.explain: Wavelength is the distance over which the wave's shape repeats (e.g. crest to crest).

questions.q: When a wave passes from one medium into another and changes speed, it may change direction. This is:
questions.explain: Refraction is the change in direction due to a change in wave speed between media.

questions.q: The spreading of a wave as it passes through a gap or around an obstacle is:
questions.explain: Diffraction is most pronounced when the gap size is comparable to the wavelength.

questions.q: When two waves meet and their displacements add, this is:
questions.explain: Overlapping waves add displacements, producing constructive or destructive interference.

questions.q: Two coherent waves meet in phase (path difference = whole number of wavelengths). The result is:
questions.explain: In-phase waves reinforce, giving a larger amplitude.

questions.q: Two coherent waves meet exactly out of phase (path difference = half a wavelength). The result is:
questions.explain: Anti-phase waves cancel, reducing the amplitude (to zero if equal).

questions.q: Only transverse waves can be polarised because polarisation requires oscillations:
options: Confined to one plane perpendicular to travel
questions.explain: Longitudinal waves cannot be polarised as they oscillate along the direction of travel.

questions.q: A standing (stationary) wave is formed by:
options: Two identical waves travelling in opposite directions
A single wave in open space
questions.explain: Superposition of a wave and its reflection creates fixed nodes and antinodes.

questions.q: Points of zero amplitude on a standing wave are called:
questions.explain: Nodes have zero displacement; antinodes have maximum displacement.

questions.q: Points of maximum amplitude on a standing wave are called:
questions.explain: Antinodes are midway between nodes, where the wave oscillates with the greatest amplitude.

questions.q: Resonance occurs when a system is driven at:
options: Its natural frequency, giving a large amplitude
questions.explain: Driving at the natural frequency transfers energy efficiently, producing large-amplitude oscillations.

questions.q: On a string fixed at both ends, the fundamental (first harmonic) has:
options: A node at each end and one antinode in the middle
questions.explain: The fundamental fits half a wavelength between the fixed ends.

questions.q: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency when:
options: There is relative motion between source and observer
questions.explain: Relative motion changes the observed wavelength and hence frequency.

questions.q: As a siren approaches you, the observed pitch (frequency) is:
questions.explain: Wavefronts are compressed as the source approaches, raising the observed frequency.

questions.q: As the siren moves away from you, the observed pitch is:
questions.explain: Receding motion stretches the wavelength, lowering the observed frequency.
